clue.text: Heap of combustible material noticed up in mountains

parts.note: a pyre is a pile of wood built for burning, as at a funeral

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for noticed is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: noticed means seen

explanation.surface: Someone spots a bonfire heap high in a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom, so the word for noticed is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the range dividing France from Spain.

clue.text: Bitter end of vendetta on island entered in record

indicators.note: end of picks out only the closing letter of the word vendetta
entered in says the island letter goes inside the record letters

parts.note: CD, compact disc, is a record

explanation.surface: The sour conclusion of a feud on an island gets written into the record books.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid and bitter are both words for a sharp, sour taste or tone.

clue.text: Vintage book about man and angel

indicators.note: about says the first pieces are placed around the word for man

parts.note: a cru is a wine of a particular vineyard or vintage
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: An old book tells of a man and an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vintage' points to the French wine term for a classed vineyard, not to age.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a child-like winged heavenly being, a kind of angel.

clue.text: Fool in ravine, nearly

indicators.note: nearly says the word for ravine loses its final letter

parts.note: a gully is a narrow ravine cut by water

explanation.surface: A foolish person stands in a ravine, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter Y from GULLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to dupe or trick them, as a fool does to a victim.

clue.text: Source of energy obtained by a large bird going over a hill

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a tern is a seabird
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Energy is gathered by a big bird flying over a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternator is a generator producing alternating current, as in a car engine.

clue.text: Bad result hurt

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A poor outcome is painful.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to wound someone's feelings, so hurt fits as a verb.

clue.text: Plant suspicion about variable air-conditioning used by hospital

indicators.note: about says the word for suspicion goes around the next two pieces

parts.note: a hint is a suspicion or trace, as in a hint of garlic
Y is an algebraic variable
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone suspects the hospital's air-conditioning is unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb in the surface (to plant suspicion) but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyacinth is a fragrant spring-flowering bulb.

clue.text: Sign of error in dodgy income we state

indicators.note: in says the cross goes inside the rearranged letters
dodgy suggests something unreliable, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A teacher's cross flags a mistake in a suspicious income declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges INCOME WE to NEWMEICO, and 'in' places X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mexico is one of the fifty United States, in the southwest.

clue.text: Elevated feeling taking place whenever in Utah

indicators.note: in says the first two pieces sit inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: UT is the postal abbreviation for Utah
PL is an abbreviation for place, as in street names
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: A good mood comes over someone whenever they reach Utah.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplift is a boost to the spirits, a rise in morale.

clue.text: Present, electronic, currently entertaining daughter

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the word for currently takes in the daughter

parts.note: now means currently
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: An electronic gift for the time being keeps a daughter amused.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to present someone with money or a gift, especially a lasting one.

clue.text: Freed from anxiety, as watchman at Elsinore thankfully was

definitions.text: as watchman at Elsinore thankfully was

explanation.walkthrough: Elsinore is the castle where Hamlet is set; a guard taken off duty is relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieved means eased of worry; in Hamlet's first scene the sentry Francisco is replaced on watch and says 'For this relief much thanks'.

clue.text: Frivolous achievement by simple artist in limited edition

parts.note: a feat is an achievement
a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
edition is cut short, limited, to the abbreviation ED

explanation.surface: An art-world triumph is printed in a short run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' is a noun here: a medicinal plant, i.e. a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherbrained describes someone silly and lightweight, with no serious thought.

clue.text: Device for regulating temperature which has queen very enthralled

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the word for which holds the next pieces

parts.note: that can replace which in a relative clause
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen
most can mean very, as in 'most kind'

explanation.surface: A gadget that a queen finds utterly captivating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled' is read literally, as held in thrall: one word holds the others captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat switches heating or cooling on and off to keep a set warmth.

clue.text: Pride in customised orange car

indicators.note: customised means altered to suit, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone takes vain pleasure in a modified orange car.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is an overbearing pride in oneself.

clue.text: Pretty small church, mostly fine

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: mostly says the word for fine loses its final letter

parts.note: nice can mean fine, as in a nice day

explanation.surface: A little church is, for the most part, lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenic means picturesque, offering a pleasant view.

clue.text: Rejected instrument, good for nothing

indicators.note: rejected suggests something thrown back, so the instrument is read backwards

parts.note: a sitar is an Indian stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A turned-down instrument is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' means sent back, so the instrument is read backwards after the abbreviation for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived for free of charge, without payment.

clue.text: Declared Scottish city excellent

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, so the city's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Stirling is a historic city in central Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish city is pronounced first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling as an adjective means of the highest quality, as in sterling work.

clue.text: Ordinary maiden overwhelmed by design of grand room once

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the maiden letter is swallowed by the rearranged letters
design of says the letters of the following words are laid out anew

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A plain young woman is swamped by the plan of what was once a great room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design of' rearranges GRAND ROOM ONCE, and 'overwhelmed by' puts M within it. A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Common or garden is an idiom for everyday, unremarkable, run-of-the-mill.

clue.text: In court, fail to keep secret

indicators.note: In says the word for fail to keep goes inside the court letters

parts.note: to lose something is to fail to keep it

explanation.surface: Someone in a law court cannot hold on to a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means hidden, not declared openly, as in a closet fan.

clue.text: Pact with soldiers previously leading to harrowing experience

indicators.note: previously says the soldiers come before the pact

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers
a deal is an agreement or pact

explanation.surface: A treaty signed with troops earlier leads to a terrible ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or trying experience.

clue.text: Not even top editor comprehends operations

indicators.note: comprehends means takes in, so the first pieces contain the operations

parts.note: a lid is a top, as on a jar
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: A chief editor who grasps the work is unbalanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is a noun here, a jar's cover, not an adjective for the editor; 'comprehends' means takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsided means uneven, with one side lower or heavier.

clue.text: Slim assembly

explanation.definitionFit: To diet is to eat less to get thinner; a diet is also a formal legislative assembly, as in Japan's.

clue.text: New volume wrapped by festive season

indicators.note: wrapped by says the volume letter is enclosed by the festive word, like a present

parts.note: Noel is Christmas

explanation.surface: A new book is gift-wrapped at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel means original, not seen before.

clue.text: Jolly part of lively revue coming up

indicators.note: coming up says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters are found within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A good bit of a bouncy stage show is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Jolly part' as the definition, but 'part of' signals the hidden word, so 'Jolly' alone defines. 'coming up' reads YREV, hidden in livelY REVue, upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly is informal British for very, as in jolly good.

clue.text: People encountering great danger

parts.note: men means people, as in men and women
ace means great, excellent

explanation.surface: People run into serious peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat or something dangerous.

clue.text: Eccentric Republican stood as candidate, dividing support

indicators.note: dividing says these pieces split the word for support

parts.note: to abet is to support or assist
to run for office is to stand as a candidate

explanation.surface: An odd Republican ran for office, splitting his backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' means splitting, so the word for support is cut open to take the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means departing from the normal, odd or deviant.
